releases.title: AutoPipeline
releases.line: Runs villa's VC3D tools and ink detection on a released scan, from surface checks to ink maps scored with controls (package, 0.1.9).
releases.summary: AutoPipeline drives villa's VC3D tools and ink detection from a released scan through surface checks, rendering and controlled scoring. Version 0.1.9 lets a plan swap any stage by name (`plan --use STAGE=NAME`) from a stage registry that lists every option with its maker, licence and maturity, and adds 3D ink readers to the ink stage, opt in and experimental: the organisers' Paris 4 3D model and published 3D predictions, read onto the same pixels as the 2.5D map with a moved-sheet control. Reader V3 stays the default reader; none of the 3D readers has beaten it on a held-out test. 0.1.8 made Reader V3 the default, and 0.1.7 drew ink maps in color. These are software changes, not a new ink-accuracy or scroll-reading result. The package retains its earlier evidence and limitations.
releases.details: Install, monitor and console, opt-in steps, synthetic demo and limitations: [README](https://github.com/ChaseHendrick/Scrolls/blob/submission/progress-2026-10-fix9/submissions/progress-2026-10-fix9/autopipeline/README.md). [Changes since 0.1.8](https://github.com/ChaseHendrick/Scrolls/blob/submission/progress-2026-10-fix9/submissions/progress-2026-10-fix9/CHANGES.md). A plan's `--use ink=reader-v3,team-3d-paris4` runs a 3D reader beside the default.

releases.title: Unroll (interactive 3D scroll viewer)
releases.line: Virtually unrolls scroll scans in 3D in your browser, with ink layers, CT tools and an Ink Bench for comparing ink models (Space).
releases.summary: [Unroll](https://huggingface.co/spaces/SharpMeow/unroll) is an interactive 3D viewer that virtually unrolls Herculaneum scroll scans with ink layers, an Ink Bench for comparing ink models, CT tools and an agent API. Status: released. Version: 1.7.0 (the Space's `version.json` and `CHANGELOG.md`). It shows nine scrolls from the Vesuvius Challenge open data, each as its traced segments with an X-ray layer, plus the published ink detection where the open data has it; PHerc. 139 also has an ink_9um (9 µm) layer over all 37 windings. The CT tools (1.2.0 to 1.5.0) add X-ray window and level with auto contrast, a CT volume view that shows a cube of the raw scan around any point of the papyrus, the traced segments drawn into that cube, and streaming from the open data bucket. Live sheet (1.7.0) streams any public segment and a CT or 3D ink volume from the bucket and shows the volume on the sheet in 3D, sampled in the browser by the same rule as `kit sheetview`. Licence: Apache 2.0 for all code; the scan data and everything derived from it are CC BY-NC 4.0. It runs in the browser with no install or account, and it can also be installed as an app that works offline. Ink layers show where models detect ink; letters visible here are candidates for expert reading.
releases.details: Opens at [huggingface.co/spaces/SharpMeow/unroll](https://huggingface.co/spaces/SharpMeow/unroll). Install app: open [sharpmeow-unroll.static.hf.space](https://sharpmeow-unroll.static.hf.space/) and press Install app in the View panel or Settings (or use the browser's install icon); the page and the default scroll then work offline. Layers, controls and credits: [`docs/unroll-space.md`](docs/unroll-space.md).

releases.title: Scroll Lens (3D DINO, ink and surface models on scan cubes)
releases.line: Shows what the organizers' 3D models (dinovol, 3D ink, recto surface) see inside a cube of a public scan (Space).
releases.summary: [Scroll Lens](https://huggingface.co/spaces/SharpMeow/scroll-lens) shows what the Vesuvius Challenge's 3D models see inside a scroll scan. Pick one of 99 ready-made cubes or a point in one of twelve public 2.2 to 2.4 µm scans, and it runs the organizers' 3D DINO embeddings (dinovol), direct 3D ink model and recto surface model on a 128³ or 256³ cube read live from the open data. The three slice views are drawn in your browser, so sliders, dragging, zoom and layers answer at once. Click a patch to light up every patch the DINO model finds alike, the organizers' own few-click recipe; the concept carries across scans and downloads as `concept.npy`. Each cube shows how well the organizers' ink reference agrees with the ink model, beside controls that must fail. A 3D view turns the three views into one rotatable space of the cube, with the slices as moving planes and ink, surface and your matches as points. For AI agents and scripts, seven tools (an API and an MCP server) list the scans and the gallery, inspect and search cubes, and download their outputs. Status: released. Version: 1.1.1. It runs on ZeroGPU and falls back to the CPU when a visitor's GPU time runs out. License: Apache 2.0 for the code; the models are MIT; the scan data and the gallery cubes derived from it are CC BY-NC 4.0. Model output, not a reading: a cube is smaller than one letter.
releases.details: Opens at [huggingface.co/spaces/SharpMeow/scroll-lens](https://huggingface.co/spaces/SharpMeow/scroll-lens); MCP at `https://sharpmeow-scroll-lens.hf.space/gradio_api/mcp/`. Source and tests: [`spaces/scroll-lens/`](spaces/scroll-lens/). Guide: [`docs/tools/scroll-lens.md`](docs/tools/scroll-lens.md).

releases.title: Inkfilter: fixed surface-volume filters
releases.line: Makes model-free maps from a surface-volume window, each with a reversed-depth control; not a trained reader (package).
releases.summary: Makes a model-free map from a surface-volume window and writes a reversed-depth control. On 56 confirmation windows from 28 publicly labelled segments across seven scrolls, face mix scored mean AUC 0.736 versus 0.704 for the selected alpha-compositing baseline and 0.628 for its reversed-depth control (Model output, 17 October 2026). Confirmation used different windows from the same development segments and scrolls. Alpha alone wins on three scrolls; the reverse filter wins on one. This is not a trained-reader comparison.
releases.details: Local NumPy, TIFF and Zarr input, synthetic tests, scalar score evidence and limitations: [package README](https://github.com/ChaseHendrick/Scrolls/blob/submission/progress-2026-10-inkfilter/submissions/progress-2026-10-inkfilter/README.md). The package needs no GPU or model weights.

releases.title: Scrolls Starter: a beginner path into the tools
releases.line: A beginner path in your browser: a synthetic practice exercise with a control, a setup checker and a Scroll Text Reader command builder.
releases.summary: A local browser introduction with a known-answer synthetic exercise, a control you can compare, a real setup checker and a command builder for Scroll Text Reader. The portable HTML works without installing Python; it explicitly leaves local setup unchecked. The guide connects our released tools and the official browser exercises to the official data notebook, VC3D and ink detection. It does not run models or download scans for you.

releases.title: Scrolls kit
releases.line: Command-line tools, benchmarks and script folders that run from a clone of this repository.
releases.summary: Command-line tools, benchmarks and script folders that run from a clone of this repository. Each line gives the tool's release date, its weights where it has them, one command to start with, its tool page and its evidence; each page lists the tool's own needs. Their outputs are model output or geometry measurements for a person to check, not readings.
commands: # The Center Finder also needs requests and torch
releases.details: `scrolls-letterdemo` downloads CC BY weights once and checks synthetic letters. Use a separate environment from AutoPipeline: both install `kit`. Every `python -m kit` command: [`docs/tools/cli.md`](docs/tools/cli.md); every tool page: [`docs/tools/`](docs/tools/README.md); a picture guide to the toolbox: [`docs/workbench.md`](docs/workbench.md).

image.alt: Concept illustration of a still life on a dark tray with a copper lip: a cube with glowing slices in front, a small papyrus roll unrolling behind it, and two cut cross-sections on a copper thread.
image.caption: Concept illustration: the toolbox's motifs on one tray. No scan data.

tools.name: Segments without VC3D
tools.line: Reads a tifxyz segment, local or from the open-data bucket, and reports its true area, grid, holes and folds, with numpy and tifffile only.
tools.summary: Reads one tifxyz segment, local or straight from the open-data bucket, with numpy and tifffile only: its true area in cm2 (checked against the area VC3D writes into meta.json), how isometric its grid is, holes, folds and stretched cells with a picture, an OBJ for Blender, a shaded preview and which way its normals face relative to the scroll's center line. On PHerc0139 w035's 2.4 um mesh: 22.07 cm2, 1.0000 of meta.json's area, no holes or folds, 43 stretched nodes, each command under 5 s on a laptop-class CPU (measured 23 October 2026). Geometry only: a clean check does not mean the trace stays on one sheet.
tools.command: python -m kit tifxyz check SEGMENT --png check.png

tools.name: Find, center line, cite and villa helpers
tools.line: Lists everything public for one scroll, fetches its best center line, prints credit lines, and checks villa PR timing and text.
tools.summary: `kit find SCROLL` lists everything public for one scroll: volumes with prize eligibility from the dated snapshot, segments per volume, the bucket's surface, lasagna and fiber predictions, center lines and public Hugging Face matches. `kit centerline get SCROLL --into FOLDER` writes the best public center line as umbilicus.json for VC3D after checking its sha256, and never overwrites one. `kit cite SCROLL` prints credit lines from metadata.json. For villa contributors, `kit prclock USER` shows the day villa's time-limit workflow would close each open PR, and `kit prtext BODY.md` checks a PR or issue body against villa's templates before posting. All read-only.

tools.name: Greek gap restoration benchmark
tools.line: Hides letters in public Greek text and scores hosted text models against a Kneser-Ney letter model under a frozen rule.
tools.summary: Hides 1 to 8 letters in 190 windows of Philodemus, De Musica (public First1KGreek text) and scores hosted text models against an order-8 Kneser-Ney letter model under a frozen rule, with a memorisation probe and a cost cap; the corpus builder and the letter model come with it, and the frozen files reproduce byte for byte. In the run of 22 October 2026 the letter model restored 0.331 of hidden letters against 0.181, 0.181 and 0.118 for DeepSeek-V3-0324, Kimi-K2-Instruct-0905 and Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct-2507, and 0.895 of single letters against 0.447 at best (Model output; one text, one prompt, one run). Public edited text, no scroll data; a fill is not a reading.
tools.evidence: [preregistration and result](docs/prereg/2026-10-22-greek-restoration.md), [frozen files, reproduction and the text's CC BY-SA 4.0 licence](docs/evidence/greek-restoration-20261022/README.md)

tools.name: Planted defect generator
tools.line: Plants sheet switches, holes and other defects into synthetic tifxyz surfaces with a known answer, to test checkers against.
tools.summary: Plants sheet switches, lenses, skips, mergers, holes and bridged holes into synthetic tifxyz surfaces (an Archimedean spiral or parallel planes) and records the winding every vertex truly sits on, so a switch detector, stack check or labeler can be tested against a known answer; `check` recomputes that truth from the coordinates alone. `kit stackcheck` is tested against it: the clean stack passes, a hole is its missing sector and a switch onto the neighbouring winding is a coincident pair. Synthetic data only; a planted surface is not a trace of any scroll.

tools.name: UV overlap gate
tools.line: Checks a flattened sheet's UV triangles for any overlap, with exact arithmetic, plus coverage.
tools.summary: Checks a flattened sheet's UV triangles (JSON or CSV) for any positive-area overlap between two triangles, with exact rational clipping behind a NumPy spatial grid, plus summed-area coverage and, with `--mesh`, one counterclockwise piece; `scripts/bench_uvgate.py` runs the overlap check on an OBJ's texture coordinates. On the released PHerc0139 w039 flattened OBJ (193,772 triangles) it passed in a median 1.0 s of gate time, 1,666 times faster than the exact reference on an 800-face prefix with identical verdicts, and caught a planted duplicate face (measured 13 October 2026). It checks the supplied UV only, not 3D sheet identity, ink or a reading.

tools.name: Relative winding consistency check
tools.line: Passes relative winding counts only when every one is an integer and all of them can hold at once.
tools.summary: Reads relative winding steps (point a to point b is k windings outward) and passes only when every count is an integer and all of them can hold at once, around every closed path across all chains, in time linear in the input, with exact integers and the standard library only. Tested on synthetic chains only; a consistent but wrong set passes, so a pass means the counts agree, not that they are right.

tools.name: Relative windings in a box
tools.line: Grows chains of sheet crossings around a point and writes villa's relative_windings.json for a spiral fit, with a VC3D plugin.
tools.summary: Grows chains of sheet crossings around a point on a published surface prediction, cuts every step where lasagna's grad_mag sees more than one sheet, and writes villa's relative_windings.json point collections for a spiral fit, with a VC3D plugin that runs it at the focus point. It needs the scroll's umbilicus and computes no prediction itself. Under readouts fixed beforehand it scored 0.9758 step accuracy on 13,969 judged steps of 18 fresh PHerc0139 boxes and, with its split rule v2, 0.9786 on 5,938 judged steps of 20 fresh PHerc1667 boxes, against the published hand windings (Model output, 24 October 2026); split rule v1 missed the PHerc1667 keep floor. It ran inside a VC3D build from the plugin branch, where a fix to keep the windings relative on load is pending.
tools.command: python -m kit windlabel-box --prediction PRED --grad-mag GM --umbilicus UMB.json --point X,Y,Z --out RUN

tools.name: Touching-sheets benchmark
tools.line: Plants sheet hops at real contacts between PHerc0139's hand-traced windings and measures how often a one-sheet check misses them.
tools.summary: Plants sheet hops at real contacts between PHerc0139's hand-traced windings w023 to w040 and measures how often a one-sheet check reading a surface prediction still joins them, and how large a window it still calls one sheet; run it on m7, recto-090 or your own prediction in m7's frame. Baselines (24 October 2026, CPU): with m7 the check joins 11 of 64 planted hops (17 %, the per-point on-sheet test 26) and keeps a median 3.5 mm square; with recto-090, 13 of 64 and 3.9 mm; neither keeps a 12.5 mm square in any of 18 clean windows. About 40 minutes on 4 CPU cores. Geometry only, never a reading.
tools.command: python -m kit hopbench refs && python -m kit hopbench run --pred m7

tools.name: Scroll Text Reader
tools.line: Proposes Greek capital letters with boxes and confidences on ink maps, drawn labels and photographs, on a CPU, with null and orientation controls.
tools.summary: Proposes Greek capital letters, boxes and confidences on ink maps, drawn labels and papyrus photographs with NumPy on a CPU, with null and orientation controls, and has an optional local Tesseract backend for Latin, Greek, Hebrew and other installed languages. On public PHerc. 1667 ink-map groups with line positions and letter height given, free-ends character error was 0.376 for `letters-v2-real` against 0.462 for `letters-v2-ccby` (Model output; 117 letters in 84 groups; those maps may benefit from training-label exposure), and photo accuracy is untested. Its output is a hypothesis for a person to check, not a reading; `--letter-px 86` suits PHerc. 1667's 38 um grid.
tools.evidence: [install, profiles and benchmarks](docs/letter-reader.md), [local OCR and session switching](docs/tools/reader-backends.md)

tools.name: Greek letter classifier and line reader for agents
tools.line: Names Greek capital letters in given boxes on papyrus photographs and reads lines of boxes, as a JSON command and an MCP server.
tools.summary: Names Greek capital letters in given boxes on papyrus photographs and reads lines of boxes with a Greek prose letter model that holds no Homer or verse, giving each letter's confidence and ranked alternatives, as a JSON command line and an MCP server for agents; the classifier is three ConvNeXt runs trained on Hell-Char only. In a preregistered head-to-head on the ICDAR 2023 test answers (8,479 letters, boxes given) its letter error was 0.291 against 0.340 for Hell-Char ConvNeXt-V2, every control passed, and as lines it was level with Hell-Char given the same letter model (Model output; photographs, not ink maps). Runs CC BY 4.0, letter model CC BY-SA 4.0, fetched once and sha256 checked.

tools.name: StrokeNet text-likeness score
tools.line: Scores how much a window of an ink map looks like lines of text, with rotation and IAAFT controls, using only NumPy.
tools.summary: Scores how much a 6.1 mm window of an organizers' ink map looks like lines of text, with rotation and IAAFT controls in every result, using only NumPy. On its preregistered held-out test on six PHerc. Paris 4 tracings it passed 7 of 9 bar items and told text from the same text turned 90 degrees far better than any simple score (AUC 0.994 against 0.865); plain ink density matched it at text against blank papyrus. `--two-density` (22 October 2026) adds a score with no network: a window's ink density plus a quarter of the density around it. On its preregistered test it came out ahead of ink density inside segments on PHerc0500P2 with ink_9um (Model output; mean within-segment AUC 0.701 against 0.662, 11 segments), a scroll ink_9um reads weakly. A score is model output, not a reading.
tools.evidence: [model card, held-out results, the tile grid pilot and the two-density score](docs/strokenet.md)

tools.name: Segment stack check
tools.line: Checks a stack of consecutive tifxyz segments against the umbilicus from geometry alone: winding order, spacing, gaps and overlaps.
tools.summary: Checks a stack of consecutive tifxyz segments of one scroll against its umbilicus from geometry alone (no CT, no model): winding order, coincident or oddly spaced neighbors, missing sectors, skipped windings, turn overlaps and stack ends, with a JSON report and per-vertex masks to drop before a spiral fit or a winding count. On PHerc0139 w023 to w040 it measured, for example, that w035 covers a median 258 degrees of its turn (measured from the published segments and umbilicus, 14 October 2026). Geometry alone cannot say which segment left its sheet.
tools.command: python -m kit stackcheck w033=SEGMENT_DIR w034=SEGMENT_DIR w035=SEGMENT_DIR --umbilicus UMBILICUS.json --out work/stackcheck/report.json --flags work/stackcheck/flags.npz
tools.evidence: [the PHerc0139 note with the full bucket example, the numbers, a CT look and the limits](docs/logs/2026-10-14-pherc0139-segment-defects.md)

tools.name: Scroll center (umbilicus) finder and coverage polish
tools.line: Finds a scroll's winding center line (umbilicus) in its CT scan with two small U-Nets and writes umbilicus.json for VC3D.
tools.summary: Finds a scroll's winding center line in its 1.2 m (about 9 um) CT scan with two small U-Nets reading level-3 slices from the open-data bucket, and writes `umbilicus.json` for VC3D and the spiral fit. Against the 13 published center lines, each scroll held out, the median distance over 3,414 slices is 0.73 mm against 3.98 mm for the centroid control (Model output, 13 Oct 2026). `kit axispolish` then moves a line to where villa's traced sheet winds most: on ten fresh scans the polished lines beat villa's vc_gen_umbilicus by +0.084 wraps of coverage, 8 of 10 scans, interval +0.028 to +0.169 (Model output, 22 Oct 2026; [evidence](docs/evidence/2026-10-22-umbilicus-windpolish/README.md)).
tools.evidence: [guide with the weight download and SHA-256](scripts/umbilicus/README.md), [evidence](docs/evidence/2026-10-14-umbilicus/README.md), [center lines for 11 scrolls with each end's check status (Model output, no person's check)](docs/evidence/2026-10-21-umbilicus-lines/README.md)

tools.name: Terminal look and mouse viewer
tools.line: Gives every kit command and script one styled terminal look, plain for pipes and --json, with a full-screen mouse viewer.
tools.summary: Gives every kit command, and every script in a Scrolls checkout, one styled look on a terminal: a title line, colour by line rules (headings, key: value, PASS and FAIL, USD amounts, clickable links), wrapping that keeps a line's own spacing, and a closing line with the exit code and time. Pipes, logs, --json and NO_COLOR get the program's own bytes. No install step: the first styled run adds a startup hook to that Python. kit live runs any command in a full-screen view with wheel scrolling, search and clickable links.
tools.command: python -m kit live -- python -m kit prizes

tools.name: Research integrity checks for Vesuvius claims
tools.line: Checks a claim before it goes out: controls on the same pixels, held-out status, number sources, preregistration and wording.
tools.summary: Checks a claim before it is posted, put in a PR or sent with a prize form: an ink score needs its reverse-depth control on the same pixels, a held-out status from that reader (from the public exposure table), the supervision mask, a number copied from its run, and an interval for any comparison; wording must not call model output a reading or call a training surface held out; a preregistration must be committed before its result and only appended to; arXiv ids and titles must match arXiv. Every command first runs 27 planted faults it must catch. Comes with a guide and the vesuvius-integrity Claude skill, which builds on the Research-Integrity skill. A pass means the record survives these rules, not that the claim is true.

tools.name: Ink map self-check (neighbor-sheet test)
tools.line: Checks without labels whether an ink map reads the traced sheet, comparing it with the same model one and two sheets away.
tools.summary: Checks without labels whether an ink map reads the traced sheet: it compares the map on the sheet with the same model read one and two sheet pitches away along the mesh normals (a map that still looks the same there is smeared across sheets or follows something every sheet shares), and flags ink that follows the mask edge or lights up empty space in the CT. Takes 2D maps read at each shift, or projects a 3D prediction volume on a tifxyz mesh itself. A pass is necessary, not sufficient: a map with no ink signal passes too, so it does not replace a labeled score with its control.

tools.name: Scroll to ink in one command (experimental)
tools.line: Experimental: one command from a public scan and a seed point to an ink map with its reverse-depth control, stopping at a failed check.
tools.summary: One command from a public scan and a seed point to an ink map: it grows a surface from the seed with VC3D, checks it for self-crossings and seating, extends it only if the extension passes the same check, flattens and renders it, and runs an ink model with the reverse-depth control, every step a Headless VC3D tool. It stops at a bad seed or a failed check, takes the layer order from the scroll's center line rather than assuming it, and resumes from one run folder, so the VC3D part and the ink part can run on different machines. Demo on PHerc0139 (in the released models' training data, so it shows the pipeline, not new ink): a 4.8 cm2 surface, check ok, about 8 minutes on Hugging Face Jobs for 0.15 USD (25 Oct 2026).

tools.name: Fast public label downloads
tools.line: Downloads a folder of the organizers' public Hugging Face datasets bucket fast, fetching each distinct file once.
tools.summary: Downloads a folder of the organizers' public Hugging Face bucket scrollprize/datasets, such as an ink label store, each distinct file once, then copies it to the other paths with the same content; the label stores are mostly copies of one empty chunk and the Hub charges by request, not by byte. On the PHerc0139 w035 ink_9um label store (3,606 files) it took 5.0 s against 61.7 s for a plain download of every file, with identical files (Measurement, one run, 25 Oct 2026). Needs huggingface_hub; no token for the public bucket.

tools.name: Swap any stage by name
tools.line: Lists every option for each stage of reading a scroll, with its maker, license and maturity, so a workflow can swap any stage by name.
tools.summary: One list of every option for each stage of reading a scroll (trace, surface, lasagna field, spiral fit, flatten, render, 2.5D or 3D ink reader, letter reader and others): who made it, its licence, its maturity (default, validated, experimental, pending, failed) and why. A workflow picks an option by name instead of hard-coding it; scroll2ink takes `--use ink=NAME` (or `KIT_STAGE_INK`) and records the pick in its settings. Unlicensed code or weights are only fetched from their own host at run time. Listing an option is not evidence that it works; its maturity and why say how far it is proven.

tools.name: Volume on a sheet in Neuroglancer
tools.summary: Samples a CT or prediction volume on a tifxyz surface and writes a mesh and Neuroglancer view. The volume and surface must use the same scan coordinates. A displayed prediction is model output, not a reading.

tools.name: Segment Atlas
tools.summary: Measures published segment meshes with the same geometry checks and builds a searchable table.

tools.name: Published segment coverage
tools.summary: Shows the heights and winding angles covered by published meshes and the gaps between them.

tools.name: Published ink labels and model exposure
tools.summary: Lists published ink label sets and the recorded training exposure of public ink models.

tools.name: Submission folder check
tools.summary: Checks a submission folder against published file requirements and lists the remaining checks for a person.

tools.name: VC3D false-404 relay and cache repair
tools.summary: Runs VC3D through a relay that retries false missing-file responses and checks its empty-chunk cache. The vc3dcache command also repairs that cache.

tools.name: Tool connection instructions
tools.summary: Writes and checks connection instructions and code examples for the public tools' hosted pages.

tools.name: Controlled ink AUC scoring
tools.summary: Scores an ink map against labeled ink and background inside a supervision mask, alongside a reverse-depth control.

tools.name: Scan catalog and batch plans
tools.summary: Lists released scan volumes, makes resumable batch plans and watches for new or changed inputs. It launches nothing.

tools.name: Run time and energy summary
tools.summary: Summarizes machine time from run provenance records, with an optional energy estimate.

tools.name: Local setup checker
tools.summary: Checks the machine and installed tools before a pipeline run.

tools.name: Ink map ensemble
tools.summary: Combines ink maps of the same surface by weighted score or pixel rank, keeping only pixels predicted by every input.

tools.name: False-404 test relay
tools.summary: Replays selected false missing-file responses through a local relay so cache handling can be tested.

tools.name: Public bucket downloader
tools.summary: Copies files under a public data bucket prefix to a local folder and skips complete files when resuming.

tools.name: Controlled benchmark gate
tools.summary: Checks recorded benchmark scores against the declared pass rules and required controls.

tools.name: Greek character language model
tools.summary: Builds and scores a character language model from public Greek text for the letter reader.

tools.name: Letter-scale ink score
tools.summary: Compares an ink map with published labels after removing broad brightness changes, with displaced-label and reverse-depth controls.

tools.name: Layer extraction and shuffle control
tools.summary: Exports surface-volume layers as images and creates a shuffled-depth control.

tools.name: Mesh and cross-scan audit
tools.summary: Checks cross-scan transforms, mesh canvases and rendering depth against public catalog geometry.

tools.name: Surface overlap and map comparison
tools.summary: Checks whether traced surfaces cover the same sheet and compares their labels or ink maps with controls. Includes the collate command.

tools.name: Synthetic map controls
tools.summary: Creates known-answer synthetic inputs for checking ink-map scoring and controls.

tools.name: Pipeline planning and cost estimates
tools.summary: Prints the official pipeline commands for a scroll without running them. The cost command adds up a run's recorded expenses.

tools.name: Public prize snapshot
tools.summary: Lists public prize requirements from a dated local snapshot.

tools.name: Run provenance records
tools.summary: Records run settings and file fingerprints, then checks the record and its files for changes.

releases.title: Umbilici (center lines of 33 Herculaneum scans)
releases.line: Every public center line (umbilicus) we know of for 33 scans, 52 lines from six sources, in 3D over the CT (Space).
releases.summary: [Umbilici](https://huggingface.co/spaces/SharpMeow/umbilici) shows every public center line (umbilicus) we know of for the 22 scans on the prize page and 11 other public scans, 52 lines from six sources, in 3D over X-ray CT that the browser streams from the Vesuvius Challenge open data, plus villa's lasagna field for PHerc0175A. Status: released. Version: 1.9.0. Each maker has its own color and any maker or single line can be hidden; 16 of the lines are model output from Chase Hendrick's Center Finder and 12 more are their coverage-polished versions, drawn as the newest with the originals faded as superseded, each scan named in a traffic light from its automatic CT end check (green pass, yellow caution or untested, red flag); the others were made by people and are credited to them. A guide covers the basics, how VC3D and villa's spiral fit read these files (cited to villa's source), every statistic and the data's frames and encodings; a Data view has sortable tables with CSV and JSON downloads, and each scan card copies file URLs, the OME-Zarr URL and a line's x, y, z at any slice. Licence: Apache 2.0 for the code; each line keeps its own licence, and the scans and lasagna field are CC BY-NC 4.0. A center line is geometry, not a reading.

releases.title: Ink Lens (control-checked ink on your own VC3D region)
releases.line: Checks one region of your own VC3D segment for ink in seconds, keeping only ink above its own reversed-depth control (Space).
releases.summary: [Ink Lens](https://huggingface.co/spaces/SharpMeow/ink-lens) checks one region of your own VC3D segment for ink in seconds. It runs an openly licensed 9 um ink model (d9v2 or `ink_9um`) on the region in three depth windows, each as stored and reversed, and keeps only ink above the region's own reversed-depth control, so a region without text comes back `none`. The result is written back as VC3D's own files: an overlay over the segment canvas, a running mosaic, `ink-detections.json` records and letter-candidate pins as a VC3D point collection. It runs on a ZeroGPU Space with your own Hugging Face token, or on your machine with `--local` (CUDA, MPS or CPU, no account), and the Space is also an API and an MCP server for agents. On the public 640 px PHerc0841 w00 sample (development data) the live Space ran 486 patches in about 1.3 s and called it `ink`, AUC 0.915 as stored against 0.595 reversed (Model output, 24 October 2026). Status: released. Version: 0.1.0. Licence: Apache 2.0 for the code; d9v2 and `ink_9um` MIT; the scans CC BY-NC 4.0. An ink map is model output, not a reading.
releases.details: Opens at [huggingface.co/spaces/SharpMeow/ink-lens](https://huggingface.co/spaces/SharpMeow/ink-lens). Try it from a clone: `python3 spaces/ink-lens/inklens.py demo 0841-w00 --score --vc3d-out /tmp/inklens-demo` (Space mode needs `HF_TOKEN` and gradio_client; add `--local` to run here). Source: [`spaces/ink-lens/`](spaces/ink-lens/); page with every option, output and failure: [`docs/tools/ink-lens.md`](docs/tools/ink-lens.md).

releases.title: Lasagna Fields (villa lasagna fields for ten scans)
releases.line: villa's lasagna fields for ten whole scans that had none in the open data, one dataset each, with a Space to view and make them.
releases.summary: [Lasagna Fields](https://huggingface.co/spaces/SharpMeow/lasagna-fields) shares villa's lasagna `predict3d` output for ten whole scans that had none in the open data, one dataset each: [PHerc0175A](https://huggingface.co/datasets/SharpMeow/pherc0175a-lasagna), [PHerc0175B](https://huggingface.co/datasets/SharpMeow/pherc0175b-lasagna), [PHerc0306B](https://huggingface.co/datasets/SharpMeow/pherc0306b-lasagna), [PHerc0483A](https://huggingface.co/datasets/SharpMeow/pherc0483a-lasagna), [PHerc0483B](https://huggingface.co/datasets/SharpMeow/pherc0483b-lasagna), [PHerc0490A](https://huggingface.co/datasets/SharpMeow/pherc0490a-lasagna), [PHerc0490B](https://huggingface.co/datasets/SharpMeow/pherc0490b-lasagna), [PHerc0841](https://huggingface.co/datasets/SharpMeow/pherc0841-lasagna), [PHerc0846A](https://huggingface.co/datasets/SharpMeow/pherc0846a-lasagna), [PHerc0846B](https://huggingface.co/datasets/SharpMeow/pherc0846b-lasagna). Each is in villa's own layout with `SHA256SUMS`; the same fields stream by URL from the public bucket SharpMeow/lasagna-fields (each card gives the URL). Made with villa's lasagna at `db3dbea2`, seams checked; raw model output. CC BY-NC 4.0, like the scans. Since 25 Oct 2026 the Space also **makes a field for any box of any public scan**: villa's own lasagna on ZeroGPU, checked against the published field (cos r 1.0 on every box tried), returned as villa's output folder from the page, API or MCP server.
commands: for f in parts/*.tar; do tar -xf "$f"; done

python -c "from gradio_client import Client; c = Client('SharpMeow/lasagna-fields', token='hf_...'); pt = c.predict(api_name='/example_points')[0]; print(c.predict(pt['volume'], pt['z'], pt['y'], pt['x'], 256, 'lasagna', api_name='/make_field')[1]['agreement'])"
releases.details: The [Space](https://huggingface.co/spaces/SharpMeow/lasagna-fields) adds region downloads, Make a field (it uses the caller's ZeroGPU time), How-to guides and an MCP server; page: [docs/tools/lasagna-fields.md](docs/tools/lasagna-fields.md). [Umbilici](https://huggingface.co/spaces/SharpMeow/umbilici?mode=lasagna&scan=PHerc0175A&z=6400) shows a sample with the center line. Model and code credit: villa's lasagna authors.

releases.title: Headless VC3D for agents
releases.line: An MCP server and shell command that let an AI agent run villa's VC3D tools with no display, checks built in (package, 1.1.1).
releases.summary: An MCP server and shell command that let an AI agent run villa's VC3D tools with no display: find open data, trace, check, render and flatten surfaces, run ink models with their reverse-depth control, drive the VC3D app, and see each result as a PNG. Version 1.1.1 serves 46 tools with JSON schemas, progress, cancellation and images over stdio, MCP protocol versions 2024-11-05 to 2025-11-25, including seven lasagna tools that drive villa's lasagna surface fit headless. The checks are built in: render votes on the surface normal before trusting the layer order, audit finds chunks a render would read as zeros, check_surface says whether a surface sits on a sheet, and target-scroll ink refuses to run without a preregistered readout rule. New in 1.1.1, docs only: the README shows every tool with a real call and its result from sessions recorded on public PHerc0139 data, a captioned replay GIF and stills, setup for Claude Code, Codex and the MCP Python SDK, and the failure modes met. It is the server that shipped inside AutoPipeline, released on its own without AutoPipeline's pipeline tools. Its tests use stand-in VC3D tools; this is software, not an ink-accuracy or scroll-reading result.
commands: claude mcp add vc3d-agent -e VC_APPIMAGE=/path/to/VC3D.AppImage -- "$PWD/.venv/bin/vc3d-agent" vc3d mcp
releases.details: Every tool with a recorded call and result, client setup and failure modes: [README](https://github.com/ChaseHendrick/Scrolls/blob/submission/progress-2026-10-vc3d-agent-1-1-1/submissions/progress-2026-10-vc3d-agent-1-1-1/vc3d-agent/README.md). The lasagna tools: [docs/lasagna-agents.md](https://github.com/ChaseHendrick/Scrolls/blob/submission/progress-2026-10-vc3d-agent-1-1-1/submissions/progress-2026-10-vc3d-agent-1-1-1/vc3d-agent/docs/lasagna-agents.md).

releases.title: dinovol embeddings of PHerc0841
releases.line: Precomputed dinovol embeddings of the whole PHerc0841 scan, to search, cluster or segment by feature similarity without a GPU.
releases.summary: Precomputed embeddings of the whole PHerc0841 9.366 um scan from the Vesuvius Challenge's self-supervised dinovol model (`scrollprize/dinovol_8um_ps192_102126`, step 640,000), so anyone can search, cluster or segment by feature similarity without a GPU. One zarr in the public bucket [SharpMeow/dinovol-embeddings](https://huggingface.co/buckets/SharpMeow/dinovol-embeddings) holds `tokens_unit` (480 numbers per 8 voxel cube), `dense` (64 per 4 voxel cube) and `ink` (32 per 4 voxel cube), int8 with a scale per vector, 539 GB; read any region by URL. Made on Hugging Face Jobs with villa's `embed_volume.py` at `4ea26d9c`; every slab read back by URL with unit-length vectors that cover exactly the scan's nonzero voxels. Raw model output, not checked by eye. CC BY-NC 4.0, like the scan. Guide and click-to-search demo: [huggingface.co/spaces/SharpMeow/dinovol-embeddings](https://huggingface.co/spaces/SharpMeow/dinovol-embeddings).
commands: python3 -c "import zarr; g = zarr.open_group(zarr.storage.FsspecStore.from_url('https://huggingface.co/buckets/SharpMeow/dinovol-embeddings/resolve/PHerc0841/20250821151531-dinovol_8um_ps192_102126.zarr', read_only=True), mode='r', zarr_format=2); print(g['tokens_unit'].shape, g['dense'].shape)"
releases.details: The [guide Space](https://huggingface.co/spaces/SharpMeow/dinovol-embeddings) (source `spaces/dinovol-embeddings/`) explains the features, has a click-to-search demo, tested download commands with sizes, and opens a whole-scan color volume (`-rgb.ome.zarr` beside the embeddings, 1.6 GB) in neuroglancer. The model's page states no license; villa's dinovol code is MIT. Credit: the Vesuvius Challenge for the scan, the dinovol authors for the model.

releases.title: Lasagnetta (experimental fast preview of villa's lasagna field)
releases.line: Experimental fast preview of villa's lasagna field; it failed one scan of its held-out test, so it ships with a self-check against villa.
releases.summary: An experimental student of villa's lasagna net: it writes a lasagna field preview in villa's own layout about 4 times faster than villa `predict3d` (59.6 s against 235.2 s on one region, RTX Pro 6000), from three small 3D U-Nets averaged ([weights](https://huggingface.co/SharpMeow/lasagnetta), CC BY-NC 4.0). **It failed its held-out test**: agreement with villa passed pooled (peak F1 0.855) but one scan of five sat under the 0.80 bar. So it ships with a self-check that runs villa's net on 12 spots and says to use villa when the median peak F1 is under 0.82. Model output; villa's own field stays the reference.
commands: pip install torch numpy numcodecs huggingface_hub
releases.details: [Tool page](docs/tools/lasagnetta.md), [source](scripts/lasagnetta/), [weights and model card](https://huggingface.co/SharpMeow/lasagnetta). The self-check (`--self-check`) needs a villa checkout (`LASAGNETTA_VILLA`). Teacher credit: villa's lasagna authors (MIT).

releases.title: Fiber Checker (are papyrus fibers visible on a traced surface?)
releases.line: A free per-patch fiber map of any traced segment or your own tifxyz, with a self-check on every run, as a Space and a command line tool.
releases.summary: [Fiber Checker](https://huggingface.co/spaces/SharpMeow/fiber-checker) renders the CT along a traced segment patch by patch and gives each patch a fiber evidence (near 1 where papyrus fibers show, near 0.5 where none do), the measure the Progress Prize asks for. The default judge is a small free model on the CPU; it passed a preregistered held-out test on PHerc0500P2 and PHerc0343P, telling the sheet from the gap beside it on every patch and from a tile shuffle on 92 to 98% (pixel measure 0.53 to 0.79). Claude with your own key is a second opinion. It does not tell which sheet a trace is on. Model output, not a reading.
commands: python -c "from gradio_client import Client; c = Client('SharpMeow/fiber-checker'); ex = c.predict(api_name='/example_segments')[0]; print(c.predict(ex['sample'], ex['segment'], ex['volume'], 60, api_name='/check_segment')[1]['summary'])"
python3 scripts/fibercheck/fibercheck.py score SEGMENT.tifxyz --ct CT_ZARR_URL --level 2 --weights fibercheck-local.pt --out out
releases.details: The [Space](https://huggingface.co/spaces/SharpMeow/fiber-checker) adds your own mesh upload, a one-page report for prize entries, a Fiber or not? game against the free judge, Compare, guides and an MCP server; `fiber.tif` sits on the segment's own mesh grid. Page: [docs/tools/fibercheck.md](docs/tools/fibercheck.md). Code and weights Apache 2.0; scans and meshes are the Vesuvius Challenge open data (CC BY-NC 4.0), read live, never copied.
